<reason>Both sides argued at a high level, but CON built the cleaner comparative path. CON conceded the harm and then offered a mechanism-matched alternative ("take the protections, leave the label"), which forced PRO to show that the gambling label does independent work. PRO's two best assets were the precautionary frame and the burden-reversal frame (consumer law regulates after the sale; gambling law refuses the sale unless adulthood is shown). CON turned that frame into a live dilemma: PRO's operational gate is a "stated age" on a platform account, which is precisely the self-declaration gambling regulators disbelieve, so either nothing changes or the identity-verification cost PRO denied returns. PRO never repaired that, even having the later closing slot available. CON also tracked PRO's definitional drift (stake/chance/prize → delivery and friction → jackpot/tiers/near-miss) and showed each successive criterion is a design variable that consumer law already governs, with the LEGO/Pop Mart rarity-tier example landing on PRO's newest test unanswered. PRO's best moment was its Q1 symmetry attack (your caps and refunds also require knowing who is a minor), but CON answered it directly and well by making the protections universal defaults requiring no age sorting. PRO scored real points on the raffled-car/"money's worth" standard, the "nobody builds that scaffolding around a Kinder egg" concession-turn, and the publisher-set exchange rate for account-bound items, which is why this is competitive rather than lopsided. CON's margin is trimmed by two clipped turns (opening and second rebuttal both cut off mid-weighing), a real execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's handling of PRO's Q1 plus the follow-on dilemma: CON showed its consumer-law package works as universal defaults needing no age sorting, then trapped PRO between a self-declared age gate (which makes the gambling label decorative) and genuine identity verification (the cost PRO spent the debate denying). PRO's answer — that platform accounts already hold a stated age — was self-undermining given PRO's own claim that gambling law reverses the default, and CON's closing exploited that directly.</best_rebuttal>
